question: The French competition authority has recently fined several professional canning associations and companies for having implemented a collective strategy to prevent manufacturers in the sector from commenting on the presence, or absence, of Bisphenol A in food containers (cans, tins, etc.).1 1.
Has the Commission investigated whether this cartel scheme has affected markets in other Member States as well?
Has the Commission considered the possibility of such methods of preventing communication on harmful chemicals being implemented for other products and chemical substances?
Will the Commission consider looking into these issues?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.5.2024) The Commission follows the investigation by the French Competition Authority. In 2022, the Commission fined metal packaging producers Crown and Silgan a total of EUR 31.

5 million for participating in a cartel concerning sales of metal cans and closures in Germany that took place in the context of the introduction of Bisphenol A–free (BPA-free) lacquers for such products.

The infringement included the coordination between Crown and Silgan to: (i) impose a surcharge, and (ii) apply shorter minimum durability recommendations concerning metal cans and closures coated with BPA-free lacquers.

The parties kept each other informed of their commercial strategies, allowing them to adapt their market behaviour and competitive efforts on the market for metal cans and closures coated with BPA-free lacquers in Germany. At the moment, the Commission does not have any pending formal proceedings on competition law grounds in relation to similar conduct being implemented for other products and chemical substances.
The Commission is monitoring any market developments closely.
